title: AI Agents Are Just Distributed Systems Now — Salman Munaf, TikTok
talk_summary: Salman Munaf argues that agentic systems are distributed systems with a probabilistic coordinator, so classic reliability patterns (idempotency, compensation, circuit breakers, budgets, scoped credentials, tracing) must wrap every tool call and agent loop. The core message is to bound, observe, and recover from agent actions rather than trusting model quality alone.

takeaways.technique: Idempotency keys and status lookup on tool calls
takeaways.what_they_do: Every external tool call carries a request id / idempotency key so retries after timeouts don't duplicate side effects; the agent can query prior request status instead of blindly retrying.

takeaways.technique: Hard budgets: max turns, max parallelism, max spend
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents get explicit caps on turns, parallel tool calls, and dollar spend so a retry loop can't run away; exponential backoff prevents retry storms against downstream APIs.
Separate read/write permissions, allow-listed tools, and approvals tied to action+timestamp+actor+expiration+parameters rather than blanket approval.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if a user has given uh an approval to approve a $30 refund, it shouldn't turn into a subsequent approval for $300 refund

takeaways.what_they_do: For each step with side effects, define an explicit compensating/undo action so a mid-workflow failure reverses prior steps across system boundaries.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It is important to reverse the entire transaction that was performed and these can uh then can cross system boundaries.

takeaways.what_they_do: When a downstream dependency is unhealthy or saturated, a circuit breaker stops agents from calling it, preventing cascading failures and retry storms.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if a downstream is unhealthy there should be system break uh circuit breakers in place that prevents AI agents to call call that dependency

takeaways.technique: Treat agent memory as invalidatable cache with provenance
takeaways.what_they_do: Classify short-term (thread) vs long-term (files, prompts, DBs, cache) memory, pick an authoritative source of truth on conflict, and invalidate cached context when the source of truth changes.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we should ideally treat memory as a cache which uh can be invalidated which can have provenence attached to it
